title: prosecutionAuthorityName is read from .prosecutionAuthorityName on cases and .name on applications

oracle.activityBoundary: every callActivity argument and return value crosses oracle/lib/boundary.js
oracle.determinismCheck: the case was run twice at clockPinIso and the two document arrays compared

edits: hearing: for every prosecutionCase, prosecutionCaseIdentifier.prosecutionAuthorityName renamed to `name`.
hearing: for every courtApplication, applicant.prosecutingAuthority.name renamed to `prosecutionAuthorityName`.
The values are unchanged — only the field each sits in is swapped, so each branch is looking at the field the other branch uses.

digests.convention: sha256 of the written file bytes — `sha256sum <file>` reproduces each value exactly

nodeEvidence.what: court application: `prosecutionAuthorityName: courtApplication.applicant.prosecutingAuthority.name` — a different field name on the same conceptual object.
whichever was found is copied to the outbound body; undefined means the key is absent.

assertion: The input is the case-and-application fixture with the two authority-name fields deliberately crossed: the prosecution case identifier is given ONLY a `name` field (its `prosecutionAuthorityName` deleted), and the court application's prosecuting authority is given ONLY a `prosecutionAuthorityName` field (its `name` deleted). Each object now carries a perfectly good authority name — in the field the OTHER branch reads. Assert EXACTLY: every document in the array has NO `prosecutionAuthorityName` key. Assert key-absent. The names are present in the input and reach the wire in neither direction, which is what makes this asymmetry load-bearing rather than cosmetic. D12 records it as a KEEP: the two field names mirror two genuinely different payload shapes. A Java port that reads `name` as a fallback — or that models both shapes with one record and one field — will emit names here and MUST fail this test. If unifying them is desired, that is a DEVIATIONS.md entry, because it changes what appears on the register.
